boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten documented no-admission, no-purchase activities for Emerson students around Boston.

cards.title: See an ArtsEmerson performance
cards.subtitle: ArtsEmerson venues, downtown Boston
cards.notes: Bring a valid Emerson ID to the box office on the performance day, then ask whether a free student ticket remains for that in-person show.
cards.short_summary: A same-day, ID-based way for Emerson students to attend an ArtsEmerson show without buying a ticket.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson students, faculty, and staff may receive one free ticket to an in-person ArtsEmerson theatre performance, film screening, or concert by presenting valid Emerson ID at the box office on the day of the event.
cards.source_title: Free/Low-Cost Resources for Students | Emerson College
cards.access_notes: Emerson ID is required; availability is determined at the box office on the event day.

cards.title: Join a library class or program
cards.subtitle: Central Library in Copley Square
cards.notes: Check BPL’s calendar, choose a no-cost class or program, and meet friends in the public library instead of planning a purchase-based outing.
cards.short_summary: Boston Public Library offers public learning and event options at no cost.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson’s student-resources page states that Boston Public Library offers events, contests, classes, and training at no cost.
cards.source_title: Free/Low-Cost Resources for Students | Emerson College
cards.access_notes: Use the BPL calendar to confirm the individual program’s date and capacity.

cards.title: Browse a free map exhibition
cards.subtitle: Boston Public Library, Central Library
cards.notes: Walk through the exhibition cases together and compare historic maps or printed materials; the library identifies its exhibitions as free and public.
cards.short_summary: A public exhibition stop inside Boston Public Library’s Central Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Boston Public Library’s exhibition procedures require all exhibitions to be free of charge and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Central Library—Copley Square Exhibition Procedures | Boston Public Library
cards.access_notes: Check current exhibitions before visiting; standard library building access rules apply.

cards.title: Look through contemporary art galleries
cards.subtitle: 20 Ames Street, Cambridge
cards.notes: Meet at the List Center, move through the galleries at your own pace, and use the free digital guide if you want prompts for discussion.
cards.short_summary: MIT’s contemporary-art galleries welcome all visitors without admission.
cards.evidence_claim: The MIT List Visual Arts Center states that it is free and open to all.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | MIT List Visual Arts Center
cards.access_notes: The official visitor page lists gallery hours and visitor policies; verify hours before travel.

cards.entity_name: MIT Museum Studio and Compton Gallery
cards.title: See a changing MIT exhibition
cards.subtitle: MIT Building 10, Room 150, Cambridge
cards.notes: Use the free gallery as a compact meet-up: view the changing exhibition, then spend a few minutes comparing one work or idea each.
cards.short_summary: A free changing-exhibition space on MIT’s campus.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Arts lists the MIT Museum Studio and Compton Gallery as open daily with free admission.
cards.access_notes: MIT lists it as open daily, 10:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; confirm access before going.

cards.title: Take in architecture-school gallery work
cards.subtitle: MIT Building 7, Room 408, Cambridge
cards.notes: Plan a short gallery stop with friends and use the surrounding common areas for conversation after viewing the current display.
cards.short_summary: A free MIT gallery near architecture studios and lecture spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Arts lists Keller Gallery in Building 7, Room 408, with free admission.
cards.access_notes: MIT lists hours as Monday–Sunday, 9:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m.; verify before travel.

cards.title: Explore biomedical images and research
cards.subtitle: MIT Koch Institute, Cambridge
cards.notes: Visit the public galleries together, read the project displays, and pick one image or research question to discuss on the way out.
cards.short_summary: MIT’s public galleries connect visitors with biomedical images and cancer-research projects.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Arts describes the Koch Institute Public Galleries as spaces for visitors to explore current cancer research, biomedical images, and related contexts; its exhibitions page identifies the gallery offerings as free admission.
cards.access_notes: Review MIT’s current exhibition information before visiting campus.

cards.title: Reserve a free MAAM visit
cards.subtitle: 621 Huntington Avenue, Boston
cards.notes: Reserve a no-cost timed ticket, then use the gallery visit as a focused afternoon activity with time afterward to talk about the work.
cards.short_summary: MassArt’s teaching museum presents contemporary art with free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: MassArt Art Museum states that it is always free and offers free tickets for visits.
cards.access_notes: Advance ticket registration is recommended; the museum notes that tickets can sell out.

cards.title: Take a self-guided plant walk
cards.subtitle: 125 Arborway, Boston
cards.notes: Choose a self-guided tour from the Arboretum’s visitor page, walk the marked landscape together, and stay on paths while observing plants and wildlife.
cards.short_summary: A large living collection with free daily landscape access and self-guided routes.
cards.evidence_claim: The Arnold Arboretum states that its 281-acre landscape is open daily and free for all to explore, with admission always free.
cards.source_title: Visit | Arnold Arboretum of Harvard University
cards.access_notes: Landscape access is daily from sunrise to sunset; follow posted visitor guidelines.

cards.title: Board USS Constitution
cards.subtitle: Charlestown Navy Yard, Boston
cards.notes: Bring required government photo ID if 18 or older, allow time for security screening, and board on a first-come basis during ship visiting hours.
cards.short_summary: A free, first-come visit aboard the active historic Navy ship.
cards.evidence_claim: USS Constitution Museum states that the ship is free to visit on a first-come, first-served basis.
cards.access_notes: The ship is open Wednesday–Sunday, 10:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m.; security screening is required, and visitors 18+ need federal or state photo ID.
